title: The Grand Opening of Twenty Twenty-Seven
skyStory: The year cracks open like a frozen pond at dawn, and the moon is already halfway through its own story, a last quarter lantern hanging in Scorpio. Scorpio does not do resolutions. Scorpio does vows, whispered, with eye contact. Saturn has arrived at the party in a sequinned parka. Mars brought sparklers nobody approved. The moon raises one eyebrow and says: fine, but make it count.

reading: Happy New Year, Tiger. You woke up with twelve resolutions already drafted in your head, and three of them involve a hammer. The [[Knight of Wands]] has read the list and circled exactly one. You know which one. It is the one that made your chest go warm when you thought of it. That is the whole year's compass, right there.

Around 11:40 am, someone will ask what your word for the year is. Do not say a word. Say a sound, like a door creaking open, and watch them laugh. Life Path 3 rule: the first story you tell in a new year sets the tone, so make it a ridiculous one with a happy ending.
joel.mission: Write your one chosen resolution on a scrap of paper, fold it into a tiny tiger, and hide it somewhere you will find it in March.
joel.omen: A neighbour shovelling in pyjamas. It means this year rewards people who show up before they are fully ready.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's fire for the first spark

reading: The year opens on your side of the calendar, Mountain. Your solstice birthday was ten days ago, so you have a head start, which you will not mention, because you are classy. The Wood Rat has already noticed who texted at midnight and who texted at 12:07. No judgement. Just data.

This afternoon the [[Six of Swords]] floats by, oars dripping. The crossing from last year into this one is not a leap, it is a row, and you may take it at a steady pace. Tell one story at dinner about the best moment of last year, and let your hands do the heavy lifting. Somebody will tear up a little. It will be a good tear.
nancy.mission: Toast the new year at the water's edge, or the nearest window facing east, and say one sentence out loud to the horizon.
nancy.omen: One perfect boot print at the very top of a snowbank, as if someone summited it at midnight. This month rewards the steady climb.
nancy.stoneWhy: clear and bright, like the first morning
nancy.elementWhy: fresh air for a fresh year

together.text: Send each other one photo of the first sky of 2027, unfiltered, no captions. Then, on a count of three, Joel moves the onyx to his giving wrist and Nancy taps her ruby twice. Equinox and solstice open the year together, and the universe is already grinning.

title: The Day of the Leftover Confetti
skyStory: A crescent moon slinks through Scorpio like a cat that knocked something off the counter and refuses to discuss it. The big night is over. The confetti remains. Scorpio wants you to find one piece of it in an impossible place and keep it as evidence that the year really started. Saturn nods slowly over a mug.

reading: The cabin is quiet this morning, chimney smoking lazily, and you will try to start a project anyway. Mars approves. The moon does not. The moon would like you to sit in a chair facing a window for twelve full minutes and do nothing except watch snow behaving.

You will find a piece of confetti somewhere it has no business being: a sock, a book, the inside of a mitten. That is your receipt from the universe for the year's first delivery of joy. The [[Six of Pentacles]] says you do not need to earn it back. Just say thanks, out loud, to the confetti. Yes, really.
joel.mission: Spend twelve minutes by a window doing nothing. Set a timer. If you reach for your phone, the snow wins a point.
joel.omen: A chickadee landing on something metal at 2:15 pm. It means a plan you shelved last year wants back on the table, gently.
joel.elementWhy: a slow day in heavy boots

reading: Wood Rat, your radar is extra sharp today, and it will pick up something everyone else misses: a small kindness across a room, a clerk humming the very tune you were thinking. Write it down. It is the first entry in a collection you did not know you were starting.

The [[Nine of Cups]] tries to whisper that you should want something shinier this year. Ignore it politely. The wish you already have, the one about helping people level up, is the real one. By evening somebody will message to say a thing you taught them actually worked. Screenshot it. Save it in a folder called Proof.
nancy.mission: Start a list titled Things Nobody Else Noticed and add three entries before bed.
nancy.omen: Someone whistling off key in a hallway. It means a door you knocked on in December is about to open.
nancy.stoneWhy: soft light for a soft day

together.text: Declare January second an official Do Nothing Summit. Each of you reports one thing you did not do today and how proud you are of not doing it. Saturn will chair the meeting. Mars will be asked to leave twice.

title: The Return of the Lost Mitten
skyStory: The moon is down to a thin ribbon, still curled up in Scorpio and refusing to leave. Scorpio likes secrets, and tonight it is sitting on a big one: something lost in December is ready to be found. The moon will not say what. It only taps its nose twice and drifts behind a cloud shaped like a kettle.

reading: Somewhere in your world there is a single mitten, glove or sock that lost its partner in the holiday chaos. Today it comes home. You will find it in a coat pocket you swear you checked, and you will hold it up like a trophy. The Tiger roars quietly. Victory is victory.

Later, the [[Knight of Pentacles]] trots by and suggests you finish one tiny chore you have been dodging, like the burnt-out bulb in the hallway. Do it before 4 pm. The light that comes on afterward is symbolic, obviously, and also just useful. Tell somebody about it with far too much drama.
joel.mission: Narrate one boring chore today like a nature documentary host, in a hushed voice, for at least thirty seconds.
joel.omen: A lone mitten on a fence post. It means someone in your life is waiting to be found and would love a message.

reading: The shore is frozen at the edges today, lace ice along the rocks, and you will feel like a detective. Something is off in a small, delightful way. Maybe a picture frame tilted. Maybe a word in an email spelled like a sneeze. The Wood Rat in you cannot leave it alone, and should not.

So here is the plan: fix one tiny wrongness with full ceremony. Straighten the frame. Correct the typo. Then announce it to the room, even if the room is empty. The [[Eight of Swords]] is a cage made of thoughts, and nothing bends its bars like doing one small thing completely.
nancy.mission: Find one thing that is slightly crooked, straighten it, and then bow to it.
nancy.omen: Lace ice shaped like a letter of the alphabet. It is the initial of someone who will make you laugh this week.

together.text: Hide a tiny surprise for the other person to discover later: a silly voice note scheduled for tomorrow morning, a doodle tucked in a shared document, a riddle with no answer. Do not mention it. Let the universe handle the delivery.

title: The Day the Compass Spun
skyStory: The moon has slipped out of Scorpio and into Sagittarius, which means it packed a bag, forgot its toothbrush, and is now humming on the highway. Sagittarius wants adventure. It is January in Atlantic Canada. Adventure will have to mean a new route to work, a different mug, a fresh playlist. Saturn approves of the mug.

reading: First real Monday of the year, and your inbox has been breeding over the holidays. Mars is side-eyeing it with real menace. Do not attack it all at once. The [[Knight of Wands]] says aim the fire at one thread, finish it, and let the rest watch you do it.

Take a different route somewhere today, even if it is only the long way to the kitchen. Sagittarius rewards novelty, and around 1:30 pm the new path will show you something small and funny: a snowman in a traffic cone hat, or a sign with a typo so good you have to photograph it.
joel.mission: Take a route you have never taken to any destination today, and name it after yourself.
joel.omen: A snowman with an unusual accessory. It means a creative idea is coming from an unexpected direction this week.
joel.stoneWhy: calm water for a busy inbox

reading: Sagittarius sends you an arrow this morning, and it lands on a question you have been carrying around since autumn. You do not have to answer it today. You only have to say it out loud to someone you trust, and watch it get smaller in the light.

Your Life Path 11 hum is turned up today. At least twice you will know what someone is going to say a second before they say it. Do not spook them by finishing their sentences. Just smile the Wood Rat smile and let them have their moment. Later, doodle the [[Ace of Wands]] on a sticky note, because something is about to start.
nancy.mission: Say your autumn question out loud to one trusted person, then ask them for theirs.
nancy.omen: An arrow drawn in frost on a car window. It means you are pointed exactly the right way.

together.text: Pick one shared goal for January, small enough to fit on a sticky note. Write it on two notes, one each, and stick them somewhere you will see daily. Saturn will check in on the fifteenth. Mars will check in every eleven minutes. Ignore Mars.

title: Don't Even Scream: The Narwhal Incident
skyStory: The moon is nearly gone, a four percent sliver dozing in Sagittarius, and when the moon naps the coincidence department works overtime. Sagittarius has fired an arrow with two names written on it. It will land somewhere between the cabin and the shore before supper. The candle leans forward. Something absurd is coming, and everyone in the sky knows it.

reading: Today you will think, for no reason at all, about a narwhal. Maybe it shows up on a kid's sweater, maybe in a crossword clue, maybe your brain just serves it up while you wait for the kettle. Hold onto that narwhal. Do not tell anybody yet.

Around 4:20 pm, Nancy will bring up a narwhal too, unprompted, in a story that has nothing to do with whales. Don't even scream. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is spinning on the tusk of a sea unicorn now. Reply with a hand-drawn narwhal, as bad as possible. Quality is not the point. Proof is.
joel.mission: Draw a narwhal in under thirty seconds, badly, and keep it in your pocket until evening.
joel.omen: Something spiral-shaped in an ordinary place, like a shell or a screw. It means the promised coincidence is right on time.
joel.stoneWhy: a single bright point, like a tusk

reading: The shore is grey and quiet, and you will feel a funny pull toward sea creatures today. A picture on a mug. A word in a book. A child at the next table explaining narwhals to an adult who did not ask. Your Wood Rat ears will catch every word.

When the coincidence lands, and it will, you are allowed one small, dignified gasp. ΔΕΣ is rarely this specific, and the universe is clearly showing off. Tell Joel the full story with both hands, tusk gestures encouraged. The [[Two of Cups]] says some links are just funny on purpose.
nancy.mission: Tell a story today that includes an animal impression, and commit to it fully.
nancy.omen: A child explaining a fact to an adult. It means someone will soon ask you for advice, and you will nail it.
nancy.stoneWhy: from the sea, like today's guest

together.text: Tonight, each of you names the sea creature you would be if the universe handed out ocean spirits. No explaining until both have answered. Compare. If you picked the same one, that is two DES events in a single day and you must both lie down.

title: The Mountain Gets the Dark Sky
skyStory: New moon in Capricorn. The moon has gone completely dark, and of all the rooms in the sky it chose Nancy's, which is either a compliment or a very long sleepover. Saturn, Capricorn's ruler, has tidied the guest room, folded the towels into tiny mountains, and left a ruby on the pillow. Seeds planted tonight grow slowly and never quit.

reading: The moon is staying at Nancy's place this week, which means your job is to be a very good neighbour. Shovel the metaphorical walkway. Carry over the metaphorical casserole. In plain terms: send her one message today that asks for nothing and gives a little something.

In your own world, the dark moon wants you to plant one idea and then leave it alone. This is hard for a Fire Tiger. You like to dig seeds up to check on them. Write the idea on paper, tuck it under the onyx bracelet overnight, and do not look at it again until the full moon on the twenty-second.
joel.mission: Write one idea on paper, tuck it under your onyx overnight, and promise not to reread it until January 22.
joel.omen: A single light left on in a dark house down the road. It means someone is thinking of you kindly tonight.

reading: The moon has come home to Capricorn, and the sky has rolled out a dark velvet carpet in your honour. Saturn bows. You get to set intentions tonight with home-field advantage, which means whatever you plant now roots deep. Choose carefully, but do not overthink it.

The [[Six of Swords]] is quiet today, the boat resting at the dock. The crossing is still happening, but tonight you get to sit on the bench and look at the stars. Write three intentions: one practical, one generous, one totally silly. The silly one matters most. Saturn needs to learn to laugh.
nancy.mission: Write three intentions tonight: one practical, one generous, and one completely ridiculous.
nancy.omen: A star you can see from your window between 8 and 9 pm. Pick it. It is yours for the year.

together.text: Both of you step outside for sixty seconds after dark and look at the spot where the moon would be. You will see nothing. That is the point. Say one wish into the dark at the same moment, by text countdown. The new moon keeps excellent secrets.

title: Zero Percent Moon, Full Volume Stars
skyStory: Zero percent moon. Not a sliver, not a whisper. The moon is lying flat on its back in Capricorn, staring at the ceiling, planning the whole year in silence. Saturn has brought it a clipboard. The stars, finally free of competition, are showing off like a choir with no conductor. Somewhere off the coast, the sea is flat as slate and listening.

reading: You will have a brilliant idea before 10 am today and immediately want to tell five people. Tell one. Only one. The dark moon likes ideas that get to grow in private before they meet the world. The [[Knight of Wands]] is pacing, but trust me, he loves a slow reveal.

Around midday you might feel like you are not doing enough. That is a fib told by the [[Eight of Swords]], which builds cages out of to-do lists. Look at your hands. They built things last year. They will build things this year. Today they are allowed to just hold a warm drink.
joel.mission: Keep one exciting idea completely secret all day, telling no one, not even a notebook.
joel.omen: A kettle that dawdles forever and then sings all at once. The slow thing you are waiting on is nearly ready.
joel.stoneWhy: many small lights in the dark

reading: Second night of the dark moon in your sign, and the shore is so still you can hear ice ticking against the rocks. Today the universe hands you the gift of a quiet hour. Nobody will need you for exactly sixty minutes. Notice when it starts. Use it however you want.

[[The High Priestess]] sits at the edge of the water with a finger on her lips. Your intuition, the Life Path 11 kind, is so clear today it is almost loud. If a name pops into your head around 3 pm, send that person a message. They need it, and they will tell you why.
nancy.mission: When a name pops into your head for no reason today, message that person within five minutes.
nancy.omen: Ice ticking or creaking somewhere nearby. It means a stuck situation is starting, very quietly, to move.

together.text: Trade one quiet wish for the year, spoken out loud, big or small. The listener may not give advice or fix anything. The only allowed reply is: noted, and I am rooting for it. Saturn calls this the slowest high five in history.

title: The Moon Checks Out of Capricorn
skyStory: The moon is packing up its guest room in Capricorn, a one percent sliver peeking out like a nightlight. It leaves a thank-you note for Saturn, written in very small, very neat handwriting. Mars, bored all week, cracks his knuckles. The weekend is coming, the sky is waking up, and something wants to be started tonight.

reading: The woodpile at the cabin is looking good, metaphorically, and today you get to light the first real fire of the year's projects. Pick the thing you have been circling since New Year's Day and do the very first step. Not the plan. The step. The [[Ace of Wands]] is literally on fire with approval.

Around 5:45 pm, someone will thank you for something you did so long ago you forgot it. The [[Six of Pentacles]] wants you to say just thank you back, with no mumbled 'oh, it was nothing.' It was something. You are allowed to have done something good.
joel.mission: Take the very first physical step on one project, even if it is just opening the folder.
joel.omen: Smoke rising straight up from a chimney. It means your intentions are travelling straight to the right place.

reading: Your moon is leaving your sign today with a wink, and it is leaving you a parting gift: one clever shortcut. Somewhere in your routine is a step you do out of habit that does not need doing. The Wood Rat will spot it before lunch. Skip it with glee.

Tonight, tell a story. Not a work story, an old one, from when you were small and the snow was taller than you. Your hands will start dancing about thirty seconds in. Let them. The [[Page of Cups]] is listening with its chin in its hands.
nancy.mission: Find one step in your routine you can skip forever, and skip it with a little flourish.
nancy.omen: A snowbank taller than a car. It means an old memory is about to make you laugh out loud.

together.text: Plan one tiny adventure for the weekend, separately, then compare notes by text. A walk somewhere new. A different breakfast spot. A snow angel in an unexpected location. Whoever has the sillier plan wins, and the prize is bragging rights until Monday.

title: The Snow Day Inventors' Fair
skyStory: The moon has wandered into Aquarius, the sky's resident inventor, who keeps a workshop full of half-built gadgets and one suspiciously glowing kettle. Only three percent of the moon is showing, but every bit of it is wearing safety goggles. Aquarius wants weird ideas today. Not good ideas. Weird ones. Saturn, the old-school co-ruler, sighs and hands over a screwdriver.

reading: Saturday, and your inventor brain is fully caffeinated. You will look at an ordinary household object, maybe a colander or a clothes peg, and see three new uses for it. At least one of them is genuinely clever. At least one is completely unhinged. Build neither. Just sketch them.

[[The Magician]] is at your table today with every tool laid out, and the trick is choosing just one. Around 2 pm a fix will occur to you for something that has annoyed you for months, like a drawer that sticks. Rub the runners with a candle stub. Then brag about it, loudly, to the drawer.
joel.mission: Sketch three ridiculous inventions for one ordinary object and send the worst one to Nancy.
joel.omen: A clothes peg on the ground. It means a loose end is about to clip itself neatly into place.

reading: Aquarius brings a cold, bright wind off the water today, the kind that makes your eyes sparkle whether you like it or not. You will feel like rearranging something: a shelf, a playlist, a plan. Go ahead. Today you will see a better order for something everyone else thought was fine.

When Joel's terrible invention arrives, rate it out of ten with a full judge's comment. Be generous with points for audacity. The [[Queen of Swords]] sits on your shoulder today, sharp and fair and secretly delighted. Your verdict will become legend, and he will quote it for years.
nancy.mission: Rearrange one shelf or drawer into an order that only makes sense to you, and label it.
nancy.omen: Your own breath fogging into a shape. It means a fresh idea is ready to be spoken out loud.
nancy.stoneWhy: a calm surface for a busy mind

together.text: Hold the First Annual Ridiculous Invention Fair by text. Each of you submits one invention that solves a problem nobody has, with a name and a slogan. Saturn judges on practicality. Mars judges on explosions. Nobody wins, which Aquarius says is the whole point.

title: The Sunday of the First Sliver
skyStory: There it is: the first sliver of the waxing moon, seven percent of silver curling over the sea at dusk, still in quirky Aquarius. Aquarius loves a fresh start almost as much as it loves pointing out that fresh starts are a social construct. The sliver ignores the lecture and grows a hair brighter anyway, just to be contrary.

reading: Look west around 5:15 pm tonight, low over the trees, and you might catch the new crescent hanging there like a fingernail clipping from a giant. Make a wish on it. A small one. Sunday wishes should be small, the size of a mitten, the size of a good nap.

The cabin wants tending today: kindling split, boots dried by the stove, the good blanket shaken out. Do one cozy chore with full attention. The [[Four of Swords]] says rest is not something you earn by running yourself ragged. It is just Sunday. Lie on the floor for five minutes. It is surprisingly great.
joel.mission: Lie flat on the floor for five full minutes, staring at the ceiling, thinking about absolutely nothing useful.
joel.omen: A thin crescent moon low over the trees. It means a small wish made today grows all month.
joel.stoneWhy: an anchor for a lazy Sunday

reading: Wood Rat, today your cleverness takes the form of a nest. Pillows arranged precisely. A drink within reach. A book you have been meaning to finish. You will build the perfect hideout in under four minutes, which is honestly impressive engineering.

Late afternoon, a message will arrive that makes you laugh so hard you snort. Do not be embarrassed. [[The Sun]], reversed in your spread, is asking you to stop earning joy and just allow it. The snort is joy. Allow the snort. Then send one back, even sillier, to whoever made you laugh.
nancy.mission: Build the perfect reading nest in under four minutes and stay in it for at least one chapter.
nancy.omen: A dog in a coat. It means comfort is on its way, and it will arrive looking slightly ridiculous.
nancy.elementWhy: a nest is the ground hugging back

together.text: Tonight, each of you sends a photo of your coziest corner, no tidying allowed. Rate each other's nests on warmth, blanket count and general cozy aura. The sliver of moon will be watching from the west and judging very kindly.

title: The Day of the Soggy Daydream
skyStory: The moon dives into Pisces this morning, a thirteen percent sliver doing slow backstrokes through the dreamiest sign of all. Pisces does not believe in schedules. Pisces believes in vibes, puddles and the deep meaning of fog. Saturn has posted a sign that says No Daydreaming During Work Hours. Pisces has already floated past it, humming.

reading: You will drift off in the middle of something important today, maybe a meeting, maybe a spreadsheet, and come back with a fully formed idea that has nothing to do with anything. Write it down before it swims away. Pisces ideas are slippery and gorgeous, like a fish wearing a scarf.

Around 3:30 pm the [[Page of Cups]] pops up with a little fish peeking out of its cup, which is to say something unexpected and charming lands in your inbox. Do not make it a project. Not everything has to become a project, Tiger. Some things are just there to make you smile.
joel.mission: Write down the strangest daydream you have today in exactly one sentence and send it to Nancy without context.
joel.omen: A puddle reflecting the sky perfectly. It means your intuition is right about something you have been second-guessing.

reading: Pisces is a water sign and you are a shore person, so today the two of you get along famously. Fog may roll in, literal or otherwise. Do not fight it. Some of your best thinking happens when you cannot see more than ten feet ahead.

Your hands will do something lovely today: tell a story to someone who needs it, or help someone finally figure out a tool they have been wrestling with. Watch their face change when it clicks. That is your favourite thing in the world, and the [[Three of Pentacles]] knows it. Count how many times you see it before bedtime.
nancy.mission: Help one person figure out one thing today, then ask them to explain it back to you in their own words.
nancy.omen: Fog rolling in off the water around dusk. It means the answer you need is closer than it looks.

together.text: Swap your strangest daydreams of the day, one sentence each, no explaining. Then each of you writes the next sentence of the other's dream. Pisces will be thrilled. Saturn will pretend not to read it, then read it twice.

title: The Day the Clocks Gossiped
skyStory: The moon is a fifth full and floating lazily in Pisces, the sign of tides and strange little signs. Pisces has been fiddling with every clock between the cabin and the shore, nudging digits around like fridge magnets. It is not malicious. It just thinks numbers should tell stories. Saturn, guardian of time, is furious. Also, secretly, impressed.

reading: Watch the clocks today. At some point you will glance at your phone and it will read 12:22, the exact date of Nancy's solstice birthday. Then it will happen again on a microwave, a parking sign, a page number. The universe is not subtle and has never claimed to be.

Meanwhile, over on the shore, Nancy will keep seeing 3:21, your equinox birthday. DES, in both directions at once. [[The Star]] is winking from either end of the line. Send your best sighting at the exact minute the next one happens, if you can manage the timing. Mars says you cannot. Prove Mars wrong.
joel.mission: Screenshot every 12:22 you see today and send Nancy the full collection at bedtime.
joel.omen: A clock running exactly one minute fast. It means you are slightly ahead of schedule on something you were fretting about.

reading: Your sharp Wood Rat eyes will catch it first: 3:21 on the oven clock. Joel's birthday, March 21, staring at you from the kitchen. You will shrug it off. Then it appears again on a bus, then on a page number, then on a clock in a shop window.

Don't even scream. Fine, maybe scream a tiny bit into a scarf. Over at the cabin, Joel is getting 12:22 on repeat, your solstice birthday, at the same time. [[Temperance]] pours the numbers back and forth between two cups. Text him the moment your third 3:21 shows up, and watch how fast he replies.
nancy.mission: Count every 3:21 you see today on your fingers, and send Joel the final total with maximum drama.
nancy.omen: A bus or truck with 321 in its number. It means the friendship is broadcasting loud and clear today.

together.text: Tonight, compare your counts. Whoever saw the other's birthday number more times picks the next shared mission. In case of a tie, you both must say ΔΕΣ out loud at 9:21 pm, which is neither birthday but feels close enough.

title: The Deep Breath Before the Cannonball
skyStory: Last day of the moon's swim through Pisces, and it is getting restless, twenty-eight percent bright and splashing toward the edge of the pool. Tomorrow it climbs out into Aries and things get loud. Today is the deep breath before the cannonball. Saturn checks the ice on the pond. Thick enough. Mars is already lacing up skates.

reading: Your Aries moon arrives tomorrow and you can already feel it, like the hum before a thunderstorm. Use today to clear the runway. Close three browser tabs. Answer the message you have been avoiding. Put away the thing that has been sitting on the chair for nine days. You know the chair.

Late afternoon you will catch yourself standing like a superhero for no reason, hands on hips, gazing into the middle distance. Lean in. [[The Chariot]] is warming up its engine, and tomorrow you will want every horse in the stable. Tonight, turn in eleven minutes earlier than usual. Mars will complain. Ignore him.
joel.mission: Clear the chair. You know the chair. Everything on it goes back where it belongs before dinner.
joel.omen: Skates hanging on a hook or a fence. It means you are about to glide through something you expected to be clumsy.

reading: The pond near the shore has frozen into a perfect grey mirror, and today you get to be brave in a small, slippery way. Try one thing you are slightly afraid of looking silly doing. A new phrase in another language. A dance move in the kitchen. A question in a meeting.

The [[Strength]] card shows a gentle hand on a lion's head. You do not need to roar today. You just need to keep your balance with a little grace, which you have always had. If you wobble, laugh. Wobbling while laughing is the most powerful pose in the known universe.
nancy.mission: Do one thing you are a little afraid of looking silly doing, in front of at least one witness.
nancy.omen: A child skating with arms wide open. It means joy is about to beat caution, and that is excellent news.

together.text: Each of you does one tiny brave thing today and reports back in exactly five words. Not four. Not six. Five. Saturn will count. If either of you goes over, you both owe the universe a goofy selfie in a winter hat.

title: The Tiger Gets the House Keys
skyStory: The moon storms into Aries at first quarter, half lit, half shadow, all attitude. This is Joel's sign, and the moon has arrived like a guest who kicks the door open and shouts greetings at everyone. Mars, ruler of Aries, has made a welcome banner in red marker. It is crooked. Nobody cares. The cabin chimney is pumping smoke like a locomotive.

reading: Aries moon, first quarter, and the whole sky is at your back. You will feel unstoppable before lunch. Use it. Pick the scariest item on your list, the one that has been glaring at you, and pounce. The [[Knight of Wands]] has been waiting all month for this exact morning.

One note from the moon, delivered with love: do not start four new things just because you can. First quarter moons are about decisions. Decide one. Then, around 7 pm, tell somebody the story of how you did it, and add one wildly exaggerated detail. Life Path 3 rules allow exactly one.
joel.mission: Pounce on the scariest item on your list before noon, then roar quietly at your desk to celebrate.
joel.omen: A red car parked perfectly straight. It means today, your aim is true.

reading: The moon has gone off to stay with Joel for a couple of days, and it has turned his volume knob all the way up. You will feel it from miles away: a burst of messages, an idea in all caps, a plan with seventeen steps. Your job today is the oldest job in your friendship. Be the mountain.

Saturn, your ruler, and Mars, his, are shaking hands today instead of arguing. That is rare. Use it. Ask him the one question that turns seventeen steps into three. The [[Queen of Pentacles]] is right there in your pocket, practical and warm. Then go do something just for you.
nancy.mission: Turn somebody's big messy plan into three clear steps today, then take a victory sip of something warm.
nancy.omen: A ram, a goat or a sheep anywhere, even on a sign. It means Aries and Capricorn are in agreement today.
nancy.stoneWhy: a steady mountain for a fiery day

together.text: Joel shares the scariest thing he pounced on. Nancy shares the smartest question she asked. Then you swap roles for one sentence: Joel asks a careful question, Nancy pounces on an idea. Mars and Saturn will both be confused, which is very good for them.

title: Saturn's Mid-Month Clipboard Check
skyStory: Second day of the moon in Aries, and it is nearly half full, glowing like a coal someone just blew on. Aries wants speed. Saturn wants proof. Today is the fifteenth, and Saturn has arrived at the door with a clipboard, exactly as promised back on the fourth. Mars tries to hide the sticky note. Too late. Saturn already saw it.

reading: Remember that sticky note with the January goal? Saturn does. Go find it, wherever it is now, maybe under a mug, maybe stuck to the bottom of a boot. Read it out loud. Then give yourself an honest grade. Not a harsh one. An honest one. Saturn grades on effort.

Here is the Aries twist: whatever your grade, you get to sprint now. The moon is nearly half full and in your sign, which means momentum is cheap today. Spend twenty focused minutes on the goal before 3 pm. The [[Eight of Wands]] is flying through the air, every arrow pointed the same direction.
joel.mission: Find the January sticky note, read it aloud, and spend twenty uninterrupted minutes on it before 3 pm.
joel.omen: A sticky note somewhere unexpected. It means the universe is checking in, and it likes what it sees.
joel.stoneWhy: a cool head at full speed

reading: Saturn is your ruler, so when he shows up with that clipboard, he looks at you first and winks. You have been quietly making progress all month. You did not announce it. You did not post about it. You just did it, the way mountains grow: one patient inch at a time.

Today, let the Aries moon give you a little shove. Take one bold step toward the goal, something louder than usual, and tell someone about it out loud. The [[Knight of Pentacles]], reversed in your shared spread, says stop earning and allow. So let yourself be proud before the work is done.
nancy.mission: Tell one person, out loud, one thing you are proud of from this month, without adding a single but.
nancy.omen: A weathervane spinning fast. It means your quiet effort is about to show up in a big, visible way.

together.text: Hold the mid-month check-in Saturn promised. Read your sticky notes to each other by voice message. Each of you names one win and one wobble from the first half of January. No fixing. Then both say, in your most official voice, the second half starts now.

title: The Great Slow Saturday
skyStory: The moon has wandered into Taurus, more than half full now and moving at the pace of a cow crossing a country road. Taurus loves comfort, texture, warm bread and very soft blankets. It refuses to be rushed and does not understand why anyone would try. Mars taps his watch. Taurus slowly eats a biscuit, staring at Mars the entire time.

reading: After two days of the moon in your sign, the Tiger is ready for a long nap in a patch of sun. Taurus fully supports this. Today, do something slowly on purpose. Simmer a pot of soup from scratch. Sand a piece of wood. Read one page three times because you liked it.

[[The Empress]] lounges across your afternoon in a velvet robe, insisting that pleasure counts as productivity on Saturdays. Around 4 pm the cabin will smell amazing, whatever you are doing. Let someone else serve you the first bowl or cup. Receiving is a skill, and you are getting better at it.
joel.mission: Do one thing today at exactly half your normal speed, from start to finish, and notice what you notice.
joel.omen: Fresh tracks in new snow, leading somewhere you did not expect. It means the slow path is the right one today.

reading: The Wood Rat loves a good hoard, and today Taurus wants you to hoard comfort. Gather your favourite blanket, a stack of books, a warm drink, a window. Build a fortress of softness and refuse to leave it for at least an hour.

Around midday, a memory from a long-ago winter will float up: sledding, maybe, or a snow fort with a tunnel. Tell it to someone, with full hand choreography. The [[Ten of Cups]] is quietly glowing on the shelf, reminding you that the best things in a day rarely come with a price tag.
nancy.mission: Build a blanket fortress and stay inside it for one full hour, snacks and stories permitted.
nancy.omen: A cardinal on a snowy branch. It means warmth is coming toward you this weekend from an unexpected direction.

together.text: Make something warm today, separately, and send a photo of it: soup, cocoa, toast, anything. Describe it in the most dramatic critic language possible. Taurus will award a velvet ribbon to the most poetic review, and Mars will be told to sit down and wait his turn.

title: The Day of the Stubborn Jar Lid
skyStory: Waxing gibbous in Taurus, the moon swelling like dough left near the woodstove. Taurus is the most stubborn sign in the sky, and today it has decided that every lid, zipper and frozen car door must put up a fight. Nothing will open on the first try. Saturn calls it character building. Mars has already growled at a pickle jar.

reading: Something will refuse to open for you today: a jar, a stuck window, a file that will not load. Your instinct is to wrestle it. The Tiger wants to win. Here is the Taurus secret: run it under warm water, metaphorically or literally, and wait thirty seconds. Patience opens what force cannot.

Midafternoon, a slow conversation with somebody wiser than you will turn up one gem worth keeping. Write it down. [[The Hierophant]] loves a good bit of handed-down wisdom, and you, Life Path 3, are the one who gets to pass it along later. Tell it to Nancy tonight, word for word.
joel.mission: When something refuses to open or work today, wait a full thirty seconds before trying again, and hum while you wait.
joel.omen: A jar lid that pops open with a satisfying click. It means a stuck plan is about to loosen.
joel.stoneWhy: a stubborn stone for a stubborn day

reading: Taurus is an earth sign and Capricorn is an earth sign, so today you and the moon are basically wearing matching boots. Everything you build today will be solid. Not fast. Solid. Pick one thing worth building slowly and lay the first stone.

Around 11 am, someone will push on a plan of yours, testing whether it holds. It holds. You do not need to argue. The [[King of Pentacles]] sits on a throne carved from a mountain and simply waits. You do the same, smiling the Wood Rat smile. They will come around by Tuesday.
nancy.mission: Lay the first stone of something worth building slowly, even if it is a single line on a page.
nancy.omen: A stone wall peeking through the snow. It means your foundations are stronger than you think.

together.text: Each of you picks one thing that has resisted you lately, a habit, a task, a stubborn drawer, and gives it one patient, calm attempt today. Report results by bedtime. Taurus will award a tiny golden bull to whoever was more gracious about it.

title: Two Conversations at Once
skyStory: The moon hops into Gemini, nearly eighty percent bright and talking a mile a minute. Gemini is the sign of twins, gossip and seventeen open tabs. It cannot finish a sentence because a better sentence just arrived. Saturn tries to take minutes at the meeting and gives up by noon. Mars is delighted. Finally, someone who interrupts faster than him.

reading: A Gemini moon on a Monday is your communicator superpower on a double espresso. Words will come easily, maybe too easily. You will explain something brilliantly at 10 am and then explain it again, for no reason, at 10:04. Pick the better version and let the other one go.

The universe sets a wordplay trap today. Somebody will say a phrase that is, without meaning to be, a perfect pun, and you will be the only one who notices. Point it out. Gently. Then use it in an email before 4 pm. The [[Page of Swords]] is a curious, chatty messenger, and today it is wearing your face.
joel.mission: Use one unintended pun from today's conversations in a message before 4 pm, and make it look natural.
joel.omen: Two identical objects side by side, like twin mugs or matching boots. It means a second chance is arriving this week.

reading: Today you will be in two places at once, at least mentally. One part of you is doing the task in front of you. The other part is already three chapters ahead, plotting. The Wood Rat loves this mode. Let both halves work. They will meet for coffee around 2 pm with a plan.

Your storytelling gets an upgrade today. You will tell a story you have told before, but this time a new detail will appear out of nowhere and make it twice as funny. Keep the new detail. It was always true, you just remembered it now. The [[Six of Cups]] smiles at old stories made new.
nancy.mission: Retell a favourite old story today and add one new detail you only just remembered.
nancy.omen: Two crows on the same branch, cawing back and forth. It means a conversation you are waiting for will happen soon.

together.text: Have a text conversation today where each message must start with the last word of the previous one. Keep it going as long as possible. Gemini will be thrilled, Saturn will try to keep score, and whoever breaks the chain must send a drawing of a goat.

title: The Day of the Second Question
skyStory: Eighty-eight percent moon, still in Gemini, and it has developed a habit of asking questions it already knows the answers to. Why is snow white? Why do cats sit in boxes? Why does Saturn wear a cardigan in every century? The stars are getting tired. Mars, for once, is listening carefully. He has a few questions himself.

reading: Today the Tiger becomes a student. Somebody around you knows something you do not: a recipe, a shortcut, an obscure fact about lighthouses. Ask them about it, then ask a follow-up. The follow-up is where the magic is. People light up when someone asks the second question.

The [[Six of Pentacles]] is back, reminding you that receiving knowledge is still receiving. You do not need to trade a fact for a fact. Just listen, nod, and say that is fascinating, tell me more. Around 6:15 pm you will learn the best fact of the week. It will involve an animal.
joel.mission: Ask someone a question today, then a follow-up, then a third, and listen properly to every answer.
joel.omen: A blinking light on the horizon, or a picture of a lighthouse. It means guidance is shining your way.
joel.elementWhy: the second question is a kindness

reading: The fog over the shore today is the thinking kind, soft and grey and good for big questions. Here is one the moon wants you to ask yourself: what would I do this week if I already knew it would work? Answer quickly. Do not edit.

Your Life Path 11 brain is collecting clues today. Notice how often the same idea shows up from different directions: a book, a conversation, a sign on the road. By the third time, it is no longer chance, it is an assignment. [[The Hermit]] holds up a lantern and says, yes, that one.
nancy.mission: Write down your answer to: what would I do this week if I knew it would work? Read it again Friday.
nancy.omen: The same word showing up three times in one day. It means that word is a message, and you should follow it.
nancy.stoneWhy: a dark mirror for deep questions

together.text: Ask each other one question you have never asked before. Not about work. Not about the weather. Something strange and delightful, like which kitchen utensil best represents your personality. Answer honestly. Saturn will record the answers in the cosmic archive forever.

title: The Day of the Two Puzzle Pieces
skyStory: The moon crawls sideways into Cancer, ninety-five percent full and carrying its home on its back like a hermit crab with a very big shell. Cancer is the sign of home, memory and things kept in drawers for decades. Tonight, Cancer has been rummaging. Something small and lost is about to turn up in two places at once. The candle gasps.

reading: Today you will find a single jigsaw puzzle piece somewhere it has no right to be: a coat pocket, a toolbox, the bottom of a drawer you rarely open. It will be mostly blue, a piece of sky. You will have no idea which puzzle it came from. Keep it.

At some point Nancy will message you about finding a puzzle piece too. Blue. Sky. Possibly a corner. Don't even scream. Okay, a small scream is acceptable. [[The World]] clicks into place in the strangest ways. Set your piece next to the onyx tonight. Cancer says missing pieces always find their people.
joel.mission: Find something lost in the house today, any small thing, and return it to where it belongs, ceremonially.
joel.omen: A blue piece of anything in an odd place. It means a missing piece of a plan is about to appear.

reading: A Cancer moon puts you in a nostalgic mood, and the Wood Rat goes digging. Somewhere in an old bag or a bottom drawer you will find a single puzzle piece, mostly blue, part of a sky. You have no idea where it came from. Hold onto it.

Then the message arrives: Joel found one too. Blue, a piece of sky, at almost the same hour. DES. Your hands will need a minute to recover from all the gesturing. [[The Star]] is shining over two pieces from two different puzzles that are somehow the same sky. Photograph yours and send it over.
nancy.mission: Photograph your puzzle piece, or any small blue thing, next to your ruby and send it to Joel.
nancy.omen: A hermit crab, or a picture of one. It means home is wherever your people are.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's stone for a shared mystery
nancy.elementWhy: home is where the heart lands

together.text: Tonight, each of you tells the other the story of one object you have kept for years for no practical reason. A ticket stub, a button, a shell. Cancer wants the full origin story. Bonus points if your hands knock something over during the telling.

title: The Porch Light Moon
skyStory: The full moon rises in Cancer tonight, ninety-nine percent bright and glowing over the snow like a porch light left on for everyone who has ever come home late. Cancer is the moon's own sign, so tonight the moon is at home in its slippers. It is sentimental. It is enormous. It would like to hear about your feelings, please, in full.

reading: The full moon in Cancer pulls on everything watery, including the parts of you that you usually keep under a lid. Somewhere around 8 pm, a feeling will float up that you have been too busy to feel. Let it come. Tigers are allowed to be soft. It is in the fine print.

The [[Nine of Cups]] in your shadow likes to say I will be happy when. Tonight the moon answers back: how about now. Look out the window at the snow, silver and blue. Name three things that are already good. Out loud, if you dare. The moon is a famously good listener.
joel.mission: Write one thing you are ready to let go of on a scrap of paper, and leave it on the windowsill under the full moon.
joel.omen: A ring around the moon tonight. It means something you let go of will come back as something better.

reading: Tonight the tide at the shore will run high and silver, and you will feel it in your chest before you see it. The moon is in a water sign, full and generous, and it wants to give you something: an evening with nothing to prove. Take it.

The [[Six of Swords]] is still rowing, but tonight the water is calm and bright enough to see the far shore. You are closer than you think. You do not need to row faster. Just look at how far the boat has come since the solstice. Tell someone one thing you have let go of this month. It counts.
nancy.mission: Stand by a window or the water tonight for three minutes, and name one weight you are setting down.
nancy.omen: Moonlight on snow so bright you can see your shadow. It means you are lighting the way for someone without knowing it.

together.text: Tonight, each of you writes one thing you are releasing, folds it small, and leaves it under the moon on a windowsill. Tomorrow the moon is fullest, so save your stones for that. Tonight is just for letting go, and the moon is happy to carry it away.

title: The Great Leo Full Moon Recharge
skyStory: Full moon, one hundred percent, and it has strutted into Leo like a lion walking onto a stage it built itself. Leo wants applause. Leo wants a spotlight. Leo wants your ruby and your onyx lined up on the windowsill like royal guests. This is the Full Moon Recharge, and the whole sky has dressed up. Saturn wore a tie. Mars wore a crown.

reading: Big night. Remember the idea you tucked under your onyx on January 6 and promised not to reread? The moon is full. Unfold it. Read it out loud to the room. Whatever it says, it has been growing in the dark for sixteen days, and tonight Leo is ready to give it a standing ovation.

Then the recharge. Take the onyx off your wrist and set it on the windowsill in the moonlight. Nancy will set her ruby out too, miles away. Fire sign moon, fire stone, Fire Tiger. [[The Sun]], reversed in your spread, asks you to allow joy without earning it. Tonight is the allowing. Leave the bracelet out until morning.
joel.mission: Reread the idea from January 6 out loud, then leave your onyx in the moonlight overnight without checking on it.
joel.omen: A cloud passing over the full moon and leaving it brighter. It means the idea you reread tonight is ready.
joel.stoneWhy: the bracelet takes a moon bath

reading: The moon is fullest tonight, in Leo, and it wants you on stage. Leo is a fire sign, and your ruby is a fire stone, which makes your pinky ring the headliner. Before bed, slip off all five stones and set them in a ring in the moonlight, ruby pointing north like a compass needle: earth, fire, water, wind, heart. The Wood Rat knows exactly how they should be arranged.

Across the miles, Joel's onyx will be sitting in the same moonlight. Equinox and solstice, Mars and Saturn, recharging side by side. The [[Knight of Pentacles]], reversed, reminds you this is not something you earned. It is just yours. Look at the row of stones once more and grin.
nancy.mission: Arrange your stones in a ring with the ruby pointing straight at the moon, then give the ring a royal name before you photograph it.
nancy.omen: A dog or cat staring at the moon. It means the recharge is working, and the animals can tell.

together.text: Full Moon Recharge. Set your stones on the windowsill at the same minute, 9:22 pm, by text countdown. Send one photo each of the moonlit stones. Then say goodnight like royalty: grandly, with at least one ridiculous title. Leo insists on titles tonight.

title: The Encore Nobody Asked For
skyStory: The moon is still almost completely full, ninety-eight percent, and still in Leo, which means it has come back out for an encore nobody requested. It bows. It bows again. It tosses a rose made of starlight into the audience. Saturn checks his watch. Mars throws the rose back. The moon catches it, delighted, and bows a third time.

reading: Morning check: the onyx spent the night in the moonlight, and it looks exactly the same. That is how you know it worked. Put it on your right wrist, the giving side, and send a little of last night's glow over to the shore. Leave it there until lunch.

Leo wants you to perform today, so do something mildly theatrical. Read a recipe aloud like a dramatic monologue. Narrate the shovelling like a sports broadcast. Bow when somebody thanks you. [[The Fool]] is cheering from the front row in a paper crown. Nobody minds. It is Saturday.
joel.mission: Perform one ordinary task today as a full theatrical production, complete with a bow at the end.
joel.omen: Snow sparkling in the sun like stage glitter. It means your efforts are being noticed by the right audience.

reading: Your stones slept in the moonlight and are freshly charged. Put them back on one at a time, slowly, like a superhero suiting up. Pearl for water, diamonds for wind, ruby for fire and heart at once, onyx for earth. You are now fully elemental and slightly glowing.

Today Leo hands you a spotlight, and someone will ask you for a story, probably around 3:30 pm. Your hands will start before your mouth does. Let them. The [[Queen of Wands]] waits in the wings, nodding, holding a cat. Somebody will remember this story for years.
nancy.mission: Put your recharged stones back on one at a time, naming the element of each, out loud.
nancy.omen: A sunbeam landing exactly where you are sitting. It means the spotlight is yours today, so take it.

together.text: Leo is still in the room, so each of you sends the other a voice message introducing yourself like a headliner at a sold-out show. Full announcer voice. Fake crowd noise encouraged. The moon will be in the front row, still holding that starlight rose.

title: The Great Sock Drawer Reckoning
skyStory: The moon has slipped into Virgo, still ninety-three percent bright but starting to wane, and Virgo has arrived with a label maker and a very specific vision. Virgo cannot see a crooked thing without straightening it. Virgo has alphabetised the stars. Saturn is weeping with joy. Mars has hidden his sock drawer, knowing exactly what comes next.

reading: The waning moon in Virgo is the universe's way of saying tidy up after the big show. Pick one small, contained space, a drawer, a shelf, the cabin's junk basket, and sort it with total focus. You will find something you forgot you had, and it will be weirdly useful.

The [[Knight of Pentacles]] plods beside you today, slow and thorough. Usually you would race him. Today, walk at his pace. Around 2:40 pm you will find the tiny thing you have been looking for since autumn. You will say aha out loud. Nobody will hear. That is fine.
joel.mission: Sort one drawer completely, and keep the single weirdest object you find on your desk all week.
joel.omen: A perfectly straight row of icicles. It means order is coming to something that felt chaotic.

reading: Virgo is your fellow earth sign, and today it lends you its magnifying glass. The Wood Rat was already the best detail-spotter in any room, and now it is practically supernatural. You will catch a mistake before anyone else, and fix it so quietly no one will ever know.

Your helpful streak is strong today. Somebody will ask you for a hand, and you will give it, but here is the twist: ask for one small thing back. An opinion, a favour, a cup of tea. The [[Six of Pentacles]] goes in both directions, and today you practise the receiving side.
nancy.mission: Help someone with something today, then ask them for one small thing in return, out loud, without apologising.
nancy.omen: A perfectly folded towel or napkin. It means your careful work is about to be appreciated.

together.text: Each of you tidies one tiny space today, five minutes only, and sends before and after photos. The after photos must be suspiciously dramatic, with moody lighting and a caption. Virgo will judge neatness. Leo, still hanging around, will judge the presentation.

title: The Day of the Loose Button
skyStory: Second day of the moon in Virgo, eighty-six percent bright and sitting cross-legged with a needle and thread. Virgo has found every loose button in the region and wants them reattached by sundown. It hums while it works. Saturn holds the thimble. Mars, who has never once sewn anything, is watching with real respect. The waning light is soft and patient.

reading: Something small around you is loose. A button hanging by one thread. A cabinet hinge that squeaks. A wobbly chair leg. The Tiger usually ignores these until they become a whole thing. Today Virgo asks you to fix one, slowly, with your full attention. It takes nine minutes. It feels like an hour of calm.

Then coast. After a big full moon weekend, Monday wants you easy. [[The Hanged Man]] dangles from a tree, totally relaxed, seeing the world from a fresh angle. Borrow his view: look at your to-do list upside down for thirty seconds. Everything on it looks funnier from down there.
joel.mission: Fix one small loose thing today, a button, a hinge, a wobble, and give it a name afterward.
joel.omen: A single thread on your sleeve. It means a small, helpful connection is about to form.
joel.stoneWhy: patient as a needle and thread
joel.elementWhy: a soft breeze for a soft Monday

reading: The shore is quiet after the big moon, the tide pulled back, leaving little treasures at the edge of the ice: a smooth stone, a bit of sea glass, a shell with a hole in it. Today is a gathering day, not a doing day. Collect small good things, real or otherwise.

Around 1 pm someone will compliment you, probably your hands, or your stories, or how you explained something. Do not deflect it. Do not say oh, it was nothing. Say thank you and nothing else. The [[Page of Pentacles]] is studying how you receive, and today you get an A.
nancy.mission: Collect three small good things today, an object, a sentence, a moment, and tell them to Joel tonight.
nancy.omen: Sea glass, or anything that looks like it. It means something rough in your week is turning smooth.

together.text: After the big full moon, declare a soft Monday. Each of you does one thing slower than necessary and one thing kinder than necessary, then reports both in a single sentence. Virgo will tidy the report. Saturn will file it under excellent.

title: The Day of the Even Scales
skyStory: The moon drifts into Libra, seventy-eight percent bright, carrying a pair of golden scales and a very nice scarf. Libra wants balance in everything: work and rest, giving and receiving, left wrist and right wrist. It weighs every choice twice. Saturn approves of the caution. Mars thinks this is taking forever. Libra smiles at both of them and adjusts the scarf.

reading: Libra is here to talk about your wrist. The onyx lives on your left, the receiving side, and you switch it right to give. Today, notice how often you want to switch it. Every time you feel the urge to give, help or fix, check: did you also receive something today? Balance the scales.

[[Justice]] holds up her scales and asks one question: what would happen if you let someone else carry the heavy end for once? Around 3 pm, a chance will arrive to accept help. Take it. The world will keep spinning. It always does, and it rather likes you resting.
joel.mission: Keep a tally today: one mark for every time you give, one for every time you receive. Try to make them match.
joel.omen: A seesaw sitting perfectly level in a snowy park. It means your give and take are finding balance.

reading: The [[Six of Swords]] is your card, the boat crossing to calmer water, and Libra reminds you today that rowing is better with two oars. You have been pulling hard on one side lately, maybe without noticing. Notice. Let Joel row for a stretch. That is the whole point of the spread.

Libra also loves beauty, so today make one thing a little lovelier than it needs to be. Arrange a plate. Add a doodle to a note. Light a candle at 4 pm just because the sky is turning pink. The Wood Rat knows small beauty is a quiet rebellion against grey January.
nancy.mission: Make one ordinary thing more beautiful than necessary today, and do not explain why to anyone.
nancy.omen: A pink sunset reflected on the snow. It means the crossing you are making is nearer the far shore than you think.

together.text: Today, each of you names one heavy thing you have been carrying alone. Then the other offers to carry one small piece of it, even symbolically. Joel might send a pep talk. Nancy might send a plan. Two oars, one boat, steady water ahead.

title: The Half Moon Peace Treaty
skyStory: Last quarter moon in Libra, half light and half dark, the most balanced the moon ever gets. Libra is thrilled. It has arranged a formal peace summit between Mars and Saturn in the middle of the sky, with a long table, two chairs and a tray of cookies. Mars wants the bigger cookie. Saturn wants a signed agreement. Libra cuts the cookie exactly in half.

reading: There is a small standoff in your week, maybe with a coworker, maybe with a stubborn task, maybe with yourself. Today the half moon offers a treaty. Meet it in the middle. Give up one small thing you were holding onto, and see what you get back.

Around 12:30 pm you will be tempted to have the last word in something. Let the other person have it instead. It will feel weird, like wearing your bracelet on the wrong wrist. The [[Two of Swords]] lowers its blindfold and grins at you. Peace is a power move, Tiger.
joel.mission: Let someone else have the last word in a conversation today, and smile about it like you know a secret.
joel.omen: Two birds sharing a feeder politely. It means a small standoff is about to resolve itself.

reading: The half moon is a reminder that you can hold two things at once. Something can be hard and also good. Something can be finished and also still growing. The Wood Rat understands this better than anyone, and today you will explain it to somebody who needs to hear it.

Your hands will do some heavy lifting in a conversation around 2 pm, drawing the shape of an idea in the air. Watch the other person's eyes follow them. That is the moment they get it. The [[Queen of Cups]] sits by the water, nodding. Treat yourself to something warm afterward.
nancy.mission: Explain something complicated today using only your hands and five words or fewer.
nancy.omen: A half-frozen puddle, half ice and half water. It means both sides of a choice can be right.
nancy.stoneWhy: a dark half for the half moon

together.text: Share a ceremonial warm drink today, separately but at the same time, as a peace treaty between Mars and Saturn. Each of you raises your mug and states one term of the treaty out loud, such as no work talk after 8 pm. Libra will witness it.

title: Three Hearts and an Octopus
skyStory: The moon is a little over half lit, still in Libra, and Libra has been gossiping with the ocean. Libra loves symmetry, and today it has arranged a perfectly matching pair of moments for two people far apart. Both involve an eight-armed creature. Both arrive by surprise. Saturn calls it a statistical anomaly. Mars calls it hilarious. The tide just giggles.

reading: Around 10:28 am, someone will tell you, out of nowhere, that octopuses have three hearts. Maybe a coworker, maybe a radio host, maybe a child. You will nod politely and file it away. It will feel random. It is not random. Nothing about today is.

Later, Nancy will text you the exact same fact, which someone told her at almost the same minute. Don't even scream. Three hearts, two friends, one octopus running the coincidence department. The [[Three of Cups]] raises a toast with all three hearts. Reply with your best octopus impression, described in words.
joel.mission: Share one surprising animal fact with a stranger or coworker today, and watch their face.
joel.omen: Anything in a group of eight: birds, cars, icicles. It means the coincidence is arriving exactly on schedule.
joel.stoneWhy: an ocean stone for an ocean day

reading: Today an octopus fact will find you. Someone, completely unprompted, will explain that octopuses have three hearts. Your Wood Rat brain will light up, because of course it does, and you will immediately think of your five stones and the heart element. Hold that thought.

When you text Joel the fact and he replies that someone told him the same thing at the same time, you are permitted one enormous scream into a pillow. ΔΕΣ. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] has eight spokes, probably, and today every one of them points at the octopus.
nancy.mission: Draw an octopus with three tiny hearts on a sticky note and send Joel a photo of it.
nancy.omen: A stranger wearing something with tentacles on it. It means your intuition is reaching in eight directions and finding gold.

together.text: Tonight, invent a name for the octopus that orchestrated today's coincidence. Each of you suggests three names, and the final name must combine one from each list. DES events need a mascot, and this one has earned it. Saturn will put it on official letterhead.

title: The Friday of the Sealed Envelope
skyStory: The moon slips into Scorpio, just under half lit and wearing a long dark coat with too many pockets. Scorpio loves a secret, a mystery, a sealed envelope with no return address. Tonight it has one of each. The waning half moon hides its face behind a gloved hand and says, darkly, that some truths are better whispered. Mars leans in. Saturn takes notes.

reading: Scorpio dares you to be honest about one small thing today. Not a confession, just a truth: I need help with this, or I really liked what you did, or that idea does not work for me. Say it plainly, once, without padding. The Tiger is braver than it thinks.

This evening, write a letter to yourself to open on your birthday in March. Seal it. Write the date on the outside. Do not tell anyone what is inside. [[Judgement]] sounds a quiet trumpet, calling the next version of you forward. Equinox Joel will be glad you wrote it.
joel.mission: Write yourself a sealed letter to open on March 21, then tuck it where you will not stumble on it.
joel.omen: A dark envelope or parcel on a doorstep. It means a good surprise is on its way to you before spring.

reading: The shore at night is Scorpio's favourite place, black water and silver ice, everything mysterious. Today your Life Path 11 intuition is basically a searchlight sweeping the dark. You will see right through one situation and know exactly what is going on. Trust it.

The [[Eight of Swords]] tries to whisper that you are stuck. You are not. The blindfold is loose, and the swords are just painted cardboard. Take one step out of the cage today, any small step, and notice that nothing stops you. Scorpio cheers in its very quiet way, which is a single raised eyebrow.
nancy.mission: Take one small step out of a rut today, a new route, a new question, a new chair, and notice how easy it was.
nancy.omen: Your own footprints in fresh snow, leading away from the house. It means you are already further along than you feel.

together.text: Each of you tells the other one small true thing you have not said out loud yet. It can be silly, like a secret favourite word, or real, like a hope for spring. Scorpio guarantees safe passage. The rule: the listener only answers, thank you for telling me.

title: The Nor'easter Clean Sweep
skyStory: A waning moon, thirty-eight percent and fading, lurks in Scorpio behind a wall of snow clouds rolling in off the Atlantic. Scorpio loves a dramatic exit, and January is leaving the stage with a full-on nor'easter. The moon wants you to shed something tonight, like a snake leaving its old skin on a rock. Saturn has brought a broom. Mars brought a leaf blower.

reading: Snowed in, or close to it, and the cabin is the perfect place to let something go. Pick one thing that has been taking up space in your head since December. An old idea that is not going to happen. A grudge against a printer. A project you started and outgrew. Say goodbye to it out loud.

Then fill the space with something warm: a long conversation, a crackling fire, a book you have been saving. The [[Ten of Wands]] says put down the heavy bundle you have been hauling uphill. Around 7 pm you will notice the cabin feels lighter, like a room after the furniture has been moved.
joel.mission: Say goodbye out loud to one idea or project you have outgrown, and thank it for what it taught you.
joel.omen: Snow sliding off a roof in one big whoosh. It means something heavy is lifting off your plate this weekend.

reading: The Wood Rat knows a storm is coming before anyone else, and you will have everything ready: the shovel by the door, the candles in reach, the good snacks hidden where only you can find them. While the wind howls, you get to sit back and enjoy being prepared. Smugness is permitted.

Scorpio asks you to release one should today. I should be further along. I should have answered that. Whatever it is, write it down, cross it out, and draw a little snowflake over it. The [[Nine of Cups]] wish was always hollow anyway. The real wish is quieter, and it is already coming true.
nancy.mission: Write down one should that has been nagging you, cross it out, and draw a snowflake over it.
nancy.omen: A snowdrift shaped like a wave. It means the crossing you started on New Year's Day is nearly complete.

together.text: Storm night ritual: each of you names one thing from January you are leaving behind, and one thing you are carrying forward into February. Send them as a two-line message. The nor'easter will blow the first list out to sea. The second one is safe.

title: The Last Page of January
skyStory: The waning crescent moon has escaped Scorpio and bolted into Sagittarius, twenty-nine percent bright and already packing for February. Sagittarius is the archer, and tonight it has an arrow aimed straight at next month with a note tied to it. The note says: well done, January. The storm is clearing. The stars are polishing themselves for the occasion.

reading: Last day of the first month, Tiger, and you made it through thirty-one days of fires, moons and narwhals. Somewhere in a hiding place there is a tiny paper tiger with your resolution folded inside. Do not open it yet. It is waiting for March. Just know it is still there, and that you are still on course.

Today Sagittarius wants one small adventure to close the month: a snowy walk to a place you have never been, even if it is only the end of a road you always drive past. Around 3 pm the sun will break through, briefly and dramatically. The [[Knight of Wands]] salutes you. One fire, aimed well, all month.
joel.mission: Walk somewhere you have never walked before today, even a short distance, and name the spot January's End.
joel.omen: Sun breaking through clouds after the storm. It means February will open with good news.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's fire to close the month

reading: January ends on the shore, the storm cleared, the snow fresh and the water sparkling the way it only does after a big wind. You started this month ten days after your birthday, with a head start, and you used it beautifully. Quiet progress, every single day. Mountains approve.

Tonight, look back at the list of Things Nobody Else Noticed that you started on January 2. Read every entry. That list is proof that your Wood Rat eyes find magic in the ordinary. The [[Six of Swords]] has nearly reached the far shore. Wave at it. February is right there, waving back.
nancy.mission: Reread your Things Nobody Else Noticed list from January 2, and add one final January entry.
nancy.omen: Fresh snow glittering at the water's edge at sunset. It means the next month holds a beautiful surprise.

together.text: Close out January together. Each of you gives the month a grade, a title and one favourite moment, in a single message. Then pick February's first shared mission. The archer is ready to fire. Equinox and solstice, one month down, eleven to go.
